goals_summary:
I am a second-year undergraduate student at UC Berkeley focused on building a strong career in AI.

Main interests (in priority order):
- AI Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (especially practical frameworks like CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, etc.)
- Large Language Models and how to use them effectively

top_papers.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
top_papers.summary: RSI-Anything introduces a domain-general framework using predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection, addressing the challenges of recursive self-improvement. This paper matters for students interested in AI agents and multi-agent systems, as it provides a practical framework for leveraging world models in agent learning. The results demonstrate substantial gains across various domains, making it a useful paper for portfolio projects or future research.
top_papers.takeaway: Save for later – useful for portfolio project: Implement the method section's world model component to gain hands-on experience with predictive modeling in agent learning

top_papers.title: Hitting-Time Bounds for Asynchronous Q-Learning
top_papers.summary: This paper focuses on bounding the error of asynchronous Q-learning, a crucial technique for multi-agent systems. The findings are practically applicable, showing that with a constant step size, Q-learning can achieve desired performance in a reasonable number of transitions. This aligns with the student's interest in multi-agent systems, making it a relevant and actionable contribution.
top_papers.takeaway: Implement or explore the 'empirical state--action count rule' to select a constant step size for a subsequent training run, as it attains the same rate without prior knowledge of model parameters or target accuracy, and is a concrete next step for the student to work on.

top_papers.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
top_papers.summary: This paper explores how task context affects language models' component roles and activation, showing that task-dependent interactions redistribute influence across layers. The findings suggest a network view of language-model computation, which could be relevant to multi-agent systems. The results also demonstrate the potential of linear response maps to improve performance, making it a potential area for practical application in agent design and planning.
top_papers.takeaway: Save for later – useful for portfolio project, as it showcases the application of understanding task context to improve language model performance, which could be applied to multi-agent systems

top_papers.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
top_papers.summary: RATED is a reliability-aware AI agent tool retrieval framework that combines semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. It addresses the gap in existing methods by using real-time execution feedback to adapt to runtime tool failures. This paper matters for students interested in multi-agent systems and practical LLM tools, as it provides a concrete solution for improving agent reliability.
top_papers.takeaway: Skim the method section and try implementing the lightweight contextual bandit module to improve tool retrieval reliability, as this relates to multi-agent systems and tool use in practical frameworks like CrewAI

top_papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
top_papers.summary: X-AgentRed proposes a self-evolving red-teaming framework for identifying compositional failures in personal agents connecting to web services and applications. By analyzing tool dependencies and execution feedback, the framework constructs a graph of harmful tool call paths and refines them through self-improvement. This paper matters for students interested in multi-agent systems and practical AI agent development, as it addresses the need for more robust and effective red-teaming methods.
top_papers.takeaway: Save for later – useful for portfolio project: Implement the framework using a framework like PyTorch or TensorFlow, and try to apply it to a small multi-agent system to see how it works in practice.
